Azure Artifacts is the current PREFERRED CANDIDATE FOR FEASIBILITY VALIDATION of the single private npm-compatible feed required by VENTO, superseding the earlier Cloudsmith pilot preference but not selecting a production provider. Microsoft documents 2 GiB free storage PER Azure DevOps organization, unlimited package identities PER feed, and a 5000-version cap per package identity. Scope mapping through npm supports unchanged @vento/ui-web, @vento/contracts, @vento/os-context and @vento/supabase across seven planned web consumer repositories without owning public @vento on npmjs or GitHub Packages. Storage is shared and finite; published versions and upstream cached dependencies count against quota where applicable. No real VENTO feed, namespace mapping or package installation verified.

As currently documented, creation of NEW Azure DevOps organizations requires an ACTIVE Azure subscription and manual action through the web portal; existing organizations are unaffected. Free tier includes first five Basic users and 2 GiB Artifacts storage; adding paid Basic identities or activating consumption above quota can generate charges. With no existing signed-in Azure DevOps organization, linked Azure subscription or account budget verified, cannot truthfully claim a production seven-consumer configuration is cost-free. The no-cost plan must validate tenant/org ownership, actual subscription/billing settings, whether separate publisher and seven revocable read credentials fit free licensing, and hard refusal of any paid upgrade before creating Azure resources.

Preparatory design ONLY: one private feed scoped to the Azure DevOps organization is favored for shared @vento/* packages across seven GitHub consumer repositories; project-scoped feed remains possible but adds project membership controls. Access should be Specific people and verified against both feed and view visibility, never anonymous or automatically all org. Disable public upstream caching unless expressly needed to conserve 2 GiB; leave ordinary public npm dependencies on their existing source while directing @vento via scoped npm registry mapping. VENTO Shell publisher: Feed Publisher only, no owner/billing credentials; each consumer: Feed Reader only, separately revocable, with auth secrets held outside Git. Recheck the actual Basic/Stakeholder/service-principal licensing model before assuming seven separate CI readers cost zero. No exact Azure organization, project, feed ID or URL has been observed and none is fabricated.
